sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Create a rubik's cube in 3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

content.thinking:
**Designing an interactive cube page**

I need to create an interactive 3D cube page using three.js, aiming for a polished look with dark cream and lime accents. The main features will include a large center cube, a settings panel, and timeline move buttons. I'll use rounded box geometry for the cubes and a charcoal grid background with warm white typography. The header will feature the CUBO logo, keeping the layout organized with annotations and control cards for a balanced composition.

**Structuring the interactive module**

I'm considering two main columns for my layout, with the left being 1fr and the right at 340px. The stage will have the top left title and a center canvas cube. The main title at the top will read "A classic. Reimagined." while the canvas will be positioned at (x580, y460). The right panel will have controls, and I need to ensure everything is clear and user-friendly. 

I'll add some action buttons like Scramble, Reset, and Undo, and provide movement options for the cube. There will also be stats, move history, and a tutorial instruction in the footer.

**Implementing cube interactions**

I'm setting up the camera orbit with mouse controls and allowing sticker clicks to turn the cube's faces while dragging, with distinct orbit and keyboard movement. The real mechanics involve rotating animations and updating grid coordinates using quaternions. The face mapping will include U, D, L, R, F, and B. 

For scrambling, I’m thinking of queueing 20 moves without a user counter until it's done, and the timer will start on the first manual move. I need to incorporate a reset animation and manage undo history carefully, particularly for manual moves.

content.text: I’ll build a polished Three.js cube playground with animated face turns, orbit controls, scrambling, undo, and an animated solve.

content.thinking:
**Evaluating geometry rendering**

I need to consider performance metrics when using different renderers, particularly with the `setAnimationLoop` function to check performance origins. The RoundedBoxGeometry has some specific settings that clamp the radius, which impacts the overall appearance of tiles. It seems like I can get a better visual by using the ExtrudeGeometry to create larger rounded corners. This would help ensure the rounded edges look polished. Currently, the visible edges of the tiles are too sharp for my taste.

**Analyzing geometry and updates**

I'm building the Shape and ExtrudeGeometry with a bevel thickness of .008 and three segments. It looks like I can adjust the tile position by using geometry translation to fix the depth issue. I might need to reset the old pivot for the cubies and reuse tile materials without leaks, which sounds achievable.

For the updateUI, during the active pivot, I’m concerned about the orientation when the move is happening. The status might get confused if the update is called while active. Also, I found that the undo feature should work correctly even after a scramble if the history is empty.

**Planning geometry tests and bundling**

I’m thinking about running some quick computational tests on the geometry state using Node without a browser. I could create a test function to validate quarter turns when attached and solved. The idea is to simulate random scenarios and then reverse them.

In the README, I want to clarify how users can install Vite and run the dev server easily. I’ll need to include a script for npm install and a note about not needing a network for runtime. Also, I should remove any invalid CSS imports that might cause warnings during bundling.

arguments.content:
# Cubiq

An interactive Three.js Rubik’s cube with rounded cubies, animated face turns, orbit controls, and a responsive dark-and-lime interface.

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite. Entry point: `index.html`; application: `main.js`; styles: `style.css`.

## Controls

- Drag to orbit; scroll or pinch to zoom.
- Click a colored face, or press **U D L R F B**, to turn it.
- Hold **Shift** to reverse a turn; the direction button also toggles reverse turns.
- **Space** scrambles; **Ctrl/⌘ + Z** undoes.
- **Solve** animates the inverse of all recorded turns, including the scramble.
- Includes move history, session timer, reset, optional synthesized sound, and a shortcut guide.

All geometry and assets are generated locally. No runtime network requests or browser storage.

Bundle compatibility check (no build output):

```sh
npm run check
```
